evidence_manifest_name: BYS360 Canonical Commit-Bound Evidence Manifest -- EXAMPLE / HISTORICAL SAMPLE, NOT LIVE RUNTIME TRUTH
policy_note: THIS FILE IS AN EXAMPLE / HISTORICAL SAMPLE. It is never auto-loaded by the calculator: scripts/quality/bys360_score_reconcile_v1.py only consults external evidence when --evidence-file (or the BYS360_CANONICAL_EVIDENCE_FILE environment variable) explicitly points at a file, and this file is not the default for either. It is kept committed for two reasons only: (1) as a schema-valid worked example a new maintainer can read to understand the evidence-file shape, and (2) as a documented, honestly-labeled historical record of what remote evidence was actually reported for commit 9def579 during an earlier governance wave -- useful for tests/demos of the resolver mechanism, never for scoring current HEAD. A prior version of this file lived at config/quality/bys360_canonical_evidence.json with no such marker and was, in effect, treated as though it could be live runtime evidence -- but a version-controlled file describing commit X can never itself describe the commit that contains the file's own addition/edit (adding or changing the file creates a new commit Y, at which point the file's evidence for X is stale relative to HEAD=Y). This is the self-attestation/bootstrap defect this rename and marker exist to make impossible to fall into by accident: actual current remote CI evidence must be supplied at runtime via --evidence-file pointing at an untracked, externally-produced file, never by editing this committed example.

No entry was fabricated for it; it simply has no manifest match and falls through to local/no-evidence resolution like any other unlisted gate.

REMOVED after a strict remote-gate provenance re-audit (governance wave: external evidence / self-attestation closure). An earlier version of this file mapped this gate to the user's reported 'BYS360 Score 100 Quality Gate V1 = PASS' CI result, reasoning that the gate's args run tests/test_score100_handover_docs_contract_v1.py, a filename containing 'score100'. On re-audit this was judged an INFERENCE, not a direct, unambiguous name/identity match: the user's reported job name does not mention 'handover', 'docs', or 'contract' anywhere, and 'BYS360 Score 100 Quality Gate V1' is not established to be the exact, sole CI step that runs exactly this one pytest file with no broader scope. Per the no-umbrella-proof-expansion policy, an inferred filename correlation is not sufficient grounds for REMOTE_CI_VERIFIED credit. The mapping is removed; this gate now resolves via LOCAL_VERIFIED (it is a version-unpinned pytest invocation, so a correct local run still yields canonical PASS) or UNKNOWN, per the resolver's normal tier-2/tier-3 policy -- never preserved merely to keep a historical replay score unchanged.
